# Independent proof review: finite path cotensors and right fractions in cote 136

Reviewer: `/root/cote123`, GPT-6 Astra Pro; inherited effort not exposed. Run: ARCH_ALG. Date: 22 November 2026 Europe/Berlin (21 November 2026 UTC). Review type: independent whole-proof check, with a complete reconstruction of the potentially missing finite-chain step.

## Verdict

**PASS**, for the explicitly specified equivalence relation generated by coefficient-preserving strict simplicial cotensor homotopies. No Brown-category or finite-product assertion is needed. One technical convention must be explicit: the finite edge path J has at least one edge and has two distinct endpoint vertices. A literal equality can be represented by a constant homotopy on one edge. A one-vertex J would not have the required surjective two-endpoint restriction.

Accepted inputs inspected in full during this review: AQ-136-COTENSOR and AQ-136-COSPAN in checkpoint 09. AQ-136-COMPARISON was also read, including its uniformity in the simplicial set. We use that accepted theorem rather than infer comparison from an unproved exactness of inverse limits.

## 1. Finite oriented edge paths

Let J be the simplicial set obtained by joining m copies of Delta[1] in a linear chain, with either orientation allowed independently, m>=1. It has no nondegenerate simplices of degree >1. The equivalence relation generated by elementary homotopies (both orientations admitted in the relation) is exactly representable by such a finite path: concatenate the given maps into the cotensor by the universal property of the union. Intermediates need not be in the image of any fixed postcomposition.

For an admissible theory C define (P_J C)_n=C(Delta[n] x J), with all operations and the S coefficient map pointwise. This is a strict simplicial bigraded differential PD S-algebra, since it is the same compatible-section limit used on the sheets (physical p.111, footer110, scan111).

Each leaf collapse J -> J' is a simplicial retraction. On the terminal leaf edge of an oriented Delta[1], use min(s,t) to contract to the initial vertex or max(s,t) to contract to the final vertex, choosing the direction of the homotopy accordingly. This formula is the identity on the common endpoint, hence glues with the constant-in-t identity on J'. Thus each collapse is a simplicial homotopy equivalence. A finite chain of collapses contracts J to a vertex. The same remains true after product with Delta[n], which itself has its usual contraction.

Fix (w,q) and let F=C_*^(w,q). Contravariance in J carries each elementary contraction to a simplicial *linear* homotopy equivalence of cotensors. It follows that F^J has the same normalized homology as F, with no flatness assumption and no dependence on the number of edges. Therefore the horizontal cutoff mu_C(q) is a valid cutoff for P_J C.

For the vertical bound d, AQ-136-COMPARISON supplies W_C(d), independent of X, such that the vertical cohomology through d of C^(w,*)(X) is ordinary cohomology of X with coefficient S^w. Applying it to X=Delta[n] x J gives S^w in degree0 and zero in degrees1,...,d. The coefficient identification is canonical, and W_C(d) is independent of n and J. This proves vertical admissibility, and it avoids any supposed interchange of an infinite product with a tail limit.

## 2. Endpoint surjectivity and the generalized path pullback

For w>=mu_C(q), NF is acyclic including H_0=0. For every n the inclusion

k[Delta[n] x {v_0,v_m}] -> k[Delta[n] x J]

normalizes to a degreewise split inclusion of free nonnegative chain complexes, with free relative basis given by relative nondegenerate simplices. A chain map from the subcomplex into NF extends inductively on relative chain degree: its already assigned boundary is a cycle, and acyclicity provides a primitive. In degree0 assign arbitrary elements to newly appearing vertices; each ensuing degree1 obstruction is still a cycle in degree0 and is a boundary because H_0(NF)=0. Projectivity of the free source terms makes these choices linear. Dold-Kan returns an actual simplicial map. Thus

(e_0,e_m):(P_J C)_n^(w,q) -> C_n^(w,q) direct_sum C_n^(w,q)

is surjective, uniformly in n.

For strict f:A->C and g:B->C form the *algebraic limit*

E=(A x B) x_(C x C) P_J C.

The products in this expression are taken in the ambient category of strict PD algebras; they are not asserted to belong to A_k. The S coefficient maps are diagonal and constant on J. The underlying module sequence in a sufficiently high weight is

0 -> E^(w,q) -> A^(w,q) direct_sum B^(w,q) direct_sum (P_J C)^(w,q)
  -> C^(w,q) direct_sum C^(w,q) -> 0,

where the last map is (a,b,h) -> (f(a)-e_0(h),g(b)-e_m(h)). It is a module map only; the limit supplies the algebra structure. Exact normalization proves horizontal acyclicity with cutoff max(mu_A(q),mu_B(q),mu_C(q)).

For vertical degrees through d choose a finite maximum of the vertical cutoffs for A,B,C,P_J C through d+1 and of mu_C(q) for 0<=q<=d+1. The sequence is degreewise exact in that range. Taking the image I of the last map in all degrees gives a genuine short exact sequence of complexes 0->E->D->I->0, and I coincides with C direct_sum C in degrees0,...,d+1. Hence it induces the expected cohomology through d. On H^0 the map is

(S^w)^3 -> (S^w)^2, (a,b,h) -> (a-h,b-h),

surjective with diagonal kernel S^w. Positive cohomology through d vanishes. This proves E admissible with uniform-in-simplex bounds, exactly as in AQ-136-COSPAN.

## 3. Cancellation in the homotopy quotient

Let H=A_k/~, with ~ the equivalence relation generated by elementary cotensor homotopies on each Hom set. It is a congruence: precomposition and postcomposition carry every elementary homotopy to an elementary homotopy.

Suppose u f ~ u g, where f,g:X->Y and u:Y->Z. Represent the finite homotopy chain by H_0:X->P_J Z, with endpoints uf,ug. The just-proved admissible theory

E=(Y x Y) x_(Z x Z) P_J Z

receives a strict map a:X->E, a=(f,g,H_0), and the diagonal strict map delta:Y->E with constant path. Apply AQ-136-COSPAN to X->E<-Y. It gives admissible R and strict h:R->X, v:R->Y with ah ~ delta v (indeed one elementary cotensor homotopy). Projection to either Y factor gives fh ~ v and gh ~ v. Thus fh ~ gh. This proves the right-cancellation axiom even when none of the intermediate maps in uf~ug factors through u.

The remaining right-fractions axioms for all arrows are immediate identity/composition closure and the cospan axiom supplied by AQ-136-COSPAN. The precise convention is Stacks Project Definition4.27.1, right multiplicative system (RMS3 is exactly cancellation after postcomposition).

## 4. Relating the two localizations and the sheet's statement

Any functor from A_k inverting every arrow identifies elementary homotopic maps: e_0 j=e_1 j=identity and j becomes invertible, so e_0=e_1 after localization. Therefore the all-arrow localization of A_k agrees, by its universal property, with that of H.

The right-calculus equality criterion (Stacks Project Lemma4.27.14, together with Definition4.27.1) then gives, for parallel f,g,

[f]=[g] in A_k[all^-1] iff there is strict admissible h:R->X with fh~gh.

The reverse implication also follows immediately by inverting h. With AQ-136-CONNECTED-SOURCES this proves:

- the all-arrow groupoid is terminal iff (a) common admissible sources and (b_h) homotopy equalization both hold;
- over Q and the stated semilocal coefficient rings, the accepted terminality theorem yields (b_h) in this concrete, sheet-compatible simplicial homotopy notion;
- over Z, this is an exact reduction, not a proof of terminality or of (b_h).

## What is not being claimed

No literal strict equalizer has been recovered. No finite product in A_k, model structure on A_k, or point-set single homotopy concatenation operation is needed. No uniformity in the *prime set* is established by this argument. The new uniformity is with respect to simplex degree and the chosen finite interval, and it follows from the already accepted comparison theorem.
